Travel Toys

Best Travel Toys For Long Flights

By Marcus Webb · May 10, 2026 · Updated August 29, 2026

Every parent who’s flown with a young child has a story about a toy that seemed perfect at the store and lasted four minutes on the plane. This review is built specifically around long-haul testing — what actually holds attention for more than one flight, not just what looks good on a packing list.

What we prioritized

The best flight toys share three qualities: no loose small pieces that end up under a seat, no sound (both for other passengers and your own sanity), and enough open-ended play value to last more than ten minutes of novelty. Magnetic and sticker-based activities consistently outperformed anything with buttons or screens for actual attention span.

Other options worth considering

Reusable sticker books

Extremely low cost and genuinely engaging for ages 3–6, though they can generate small paper scraps that need managing on a tray table.

Magnetic drawing boards

Zero loose pieces and fully reusable, a strong pick specifically for toddlers who tend to lose or throw small items.

How it performed

Tested across four long-haul flights with kids aged 4 and 6, the magnetic building set held attention longest — noticeably longer than a tablet game, which both kids tired of within 20 minutes. The set's pieces clip together well enough that turbulence didn't scatter them.

Pros and cons

What we liked

  • No small loose pieces that roll under the seat in front
  • Genuinely silent, unlike anything with buttons or a speaker
  • Reusable across many flights rather than a one-trip novelty

Worth knowing

  • Best suited to a tray-table sized activity — not ideal for use during takeoff and landing when trays must be stowed
  • Younger toddlers (under 3) may still put pieces in their mouths, worth checking piece size against your child's stage

Frequently asked questions

What are the best screen-free activities for a long flight?

Magnetic building sets, reusable sticker books, and magnetic drawing boards all hold attention well without noise or loose pieces, based on our testing across several long-haul flights.

How many toys should you pack per child for a flight?

Two to three varied activities is usually enough — one drawing-based, one building or manipulative, and one familiar comfort item — rather than a large quantity of similar options.

Are screens better than toys for long flights?

Screens can help, but in our testing, engaging physical activities held attention longer than tablet games and don't come with the battery-life or eye-strain concerns of extended screen time.
